Report with hard evidence (file paths, function names, exact LINE NUMBERS, verbatim code):

2. Report the exact function that copies switches onto the child command line — likely `UtilityProcessHost::CreateUtilityProcess` / `StartProcess` / a `base::CommandLine` copy loop iterating a switch-name array and calling `child_command_line->AppendSwitchASCII(name, source->GetSwitchValueASCII(name))` or `CopySwitchesFrom`. Report the function name, the file, and the EXACT line number of the copy loop. Show the loop verbatim.

3. Confirm whether the network service utility process launch path actually goes through content/browser/service_host/. Chromium may launch the network service via `content/browser/network_service_instance_impl.cc` (which creates a UtilityProcessHost with service sandbox type kNetwork). Verify: grep for `network::mojom::NetworkService` / `kNetworkService` / `ServiceSandboxType` in content/browser/. State explicitly: does the same switch-propagation path in content/browser/service_host/ handle the network service, or is there a DIFFERENT process launch path (e.g. a mojom NetworkServiceParams, or services/network/network_service running in-process)? 4. Or is mojom plumbing / an extra parameter needed (e.g. does the network service get its own command line at all, vs. being passed config over mojom)? Look for whether the switch value would need to be passed via `NetworkServiceParams` or `CreateNetworkContextParams` instead. Verify by reading the actual launch code.

5. Report how a switch gets REGISTERED in the browser process so that `base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->HasSwitch(...)` / `GetSwitchValueASCII(...)` works and so the switch appears in `--help`-ish lists: find `content/public/common/content_switches.cc` (the `::switches` namespace, e.g. `const char kSomeSwitch[] = "some-switch";`) and `content/public/common/content_switches.h`. Report the exact line where a nearby switch string constant is defined and the line in the header where it is declared, so the main agent can add `kInjectCandidateId`. ALSO: report WHETHER content/public/common is a valid place — i.e. is content_switches.cc linked into the browser process AND is it accessible (a link-time dependency) from the network layer? Check the network layer side: does services/network/ have a dependency on content/public/common? Look at services/network/BUILD.gn for deps like `//content/public/common` — if it does NOT, note that a switch defined in content/public/common may NOT be linkable from services/network/, and instead the network service reads it from `base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()` using a string constant defined locally (e.g. in services/network/ or base/). Report what the safest linkable location is. Check how services/network/ currently reads browser switches — grep services/network/ for `base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()` and report examples with file:line, and note which header/constant they use. This is critical to avoid a link error.

6. Also report: is there an existing `switches::k...` constant in `content/public/common/content_switches.h` that the network service ALREADY reads? If services/network reads switches from content/public/common, that proves linkability. If not, identify the alternative.

Report "not found in this tree" for anything you cannot locate rather than guessing.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.
